name: Lesson 19 · To me, to you: dative pronouns, es gibt, two objects

cards.note: Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. helfen takes the dative, so ich becomes mir.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. With gefallen, the one who likes is in the dative: mir.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. Literally how goes it to you: du becomes dir.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. The answer keeps the dative: es geht mir gut.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. schmecken + dative: dir.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. er becomes ihm in the dative.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. sie (she) becomes ihr in the dative.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. Sie becomes Ihnen, with a capital I.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. ihr becomes euch, the same as in the accusative.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. wir becomes uns, the same as in the accusative.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. sie (they) becomes ihnen in the dative.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. wehtun: the person who is hurting is in the dative, and German uses no possessive for the body part.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. tut … weh splits like other separable verbs; dir says whose stomach.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. passen + dative: mir.
Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. Ihnen: the formal dative.

cards.front: Can you lend **me** your bike? (one friend)
cards.note: Dative pronouns: mir, dir, ihm…. leihen: to lend; the one who gets it is in the dative.
es gibt: there is, there are. es gibt means there is; in a question the verb comes first: gibt es.
es gibt: there is, there are. es gibt takes the accusative: keinen Zucker.

cards.front: **There are** a lot of restaurants here.
cards.note: es gibt: there is, there are. es gibt stays singular, even for many things.
es gibt: there is, there are. Gibt es…? asks whether something is available.
es gibt: there is, there are. gibt es + accusative: eine Toilette.
es gibt: there is, there are. es gibt ein Problem: there's a problem.
es gibt: there is, there are. hier first, the verb second: gibt es.
Two objects: which comes first. A pronoun goes before a noun: ihm (dative), then den Apfel.
Two objects: which comes first. der Apfel → ihn. An accusative pronoun goes before the dative noun.
Two objects: which comes first. Two pronouns: the accusative first, then the dative.
Two objects: which comes first. Two nouns: the dative before the accusative.

cards.front: Can you show **me** the way? (one friend)
cards.note: Two objects: which comes first. mir before den Weg: the pronoun first.
Two objects: which comes first. uns (dative pronoun) before die Frage (accusative noun).
Two objects: which comes first. Dative noun first, then the accusative noun: unserer Oma Blumen.
Two objects: which comes first. schenken: to give as a present. Dative noun, then accusative noun.
Two objects: which comes first. das Buch → es. The pronoun jumps ahead of the dative noun.
Two objects: which comes first. dir before den Schlüssel: pronoun before noun.

cards.front: I'll bring **it to you**. (the key; one friend)
cards.note: Two objects: which comes first. der Schlüssel → ihn. Two pronouns: accusative, then dative.

cards.front: The photos? I'll show **them to you**. (one friend)
cards.note: Two objects: which comes first. die Fotos → sie (accusative), then dir.

cards.front: Can you explain **it to me**? (the question; one friend)
cards.note: Two objects: which comes first. die Frage → sie, then mir, then the infinitive.
